SecondOrderDetail:
For $(22,166)$, the linear programs of Proposition~ef{prop:descent} (
olinkurl{explore9_descent.py}, untrusted) find no descent in the 4 flex directions tried (largest margin $\eta=-0.49$, where a descent needs $\eta>0$), so by duality each of these directions has a nonnegative stress with $H_\omega\ge0$ on it. For the exact strictly positive stress constant on the classes of contacts, $H_\omega$ is computed exactly on the exact flexes: for $(11,604)$ it is identically zero and for $(22,166)$ it is negative definite. Numerically (
olinkurl{explore9_classes.py}), every strictly positive stress constant on the classes of contacts makes $H_\omega$ negative definite on the flexes, so Theorem~ef{thm:second} cannot be applied with a symmetric stress. For $(11,604)$ the flexes move 492 of the 604 points (the other 112 span a subspace of dimension 8), and $H_\omega$ vanishes on them, to $4.6\cdot10^{-14}$, for every stress constant on the classes of contacts, as it must along a continuous family of configurations with the same contacts; whether such a family exists, which would make the code a local minimum that is not strict, is open. Numerically (
olinkurl{explore9_family.py}), Gauss--Newton projections along a flex of $(11,604)$ reach configurations at least 0.24 away from it (least squares, modulo $O(11)$) with every contact at cosine $1/2$ to $2.3\cdot10^{-15}$ and every other inner product at most 0.4971, so the code appears to lie in a continuous family of kissing configurations (Conjecture~ef{conj:kiss}).
SecondOrderFinding: the exact codes $(11,604)$ and $(22,166)$, the first of them the 604-point kissing configuration in $\R^{11}$ found in 2026~\cite{BKPZ26}, are not infinitesimally jammed, and neither second-order test decides whether they are jammed; numerically the kissing configuration lies in a continuous family of kissing configurations (Conjecture~\ref{conj:kiss}).
